plan.title: Simple Counter SPA
plan.design: The application uses Next.js App Router with a single page component located at app/page.tsx. The page renders a counter value stored in React state via the useState hook. An Increment button updates the state by adding one. No backend, database, authentication, or external services are involved. All state is transient and resets to zero on page reload. The default layout from app/layout.tsx is used; no modifications are required. The component is fully accessible with a visible button label and the counter value is rendered as text. No additional files or dependencies are needed.

files.purpose: Main page rendering counter with Increment button and state management

acceptance_criteria: The page displays a numeric value starting at 0.
An "Increment" button is visible and labeled correctly.
Clicking the button increases the displayed number by 1 each time.
Reloading the page resets the counter to 0.
The counter and button are accessible (visible text, proper button semantics).
plan.test_strategy: Manual testing: 1) Verify initial render shows 0. 2) Click Increment and confirm value increments. 3) Repeat to ensure consistent behavior. 4) Reload page and confirm value resets to 0. 5) Inspect DOM to ensure button is a <button> element with accessible text. Automated testing could be added with React Testing Library and Jest if desired, but is not required for this POC.
assumptions: The browser environment supports React 19.3.1 and Next.js 16.4.3.
No server-side rendering is required for this simple counter.
No external services or authentication are needed.
